skill.name: reference-builder
skill.description: Creates comprehensive technical references for APIs, configuration options, schemas, errors, examples, and migration details.
skill.summary: Builds complete API, configuration, and schema references with examples, indexes, and cross-references.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All five static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code, fenced documentation templates, and ordinary reference-documentation wording. No executable shell commands, system reconnaissance behavior, prompt injection attempt, network use, or data exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: - If detailed examples are required, open `resources/implementation-playbook.md`.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 26 contains a Markdown inline file path to a resource, not Ruby or shell backtick execution. It instructs the user to open local documentation when examples are needed.
Lines 64-77 start a fenced Markdown template for a documentation entry. The backticks delimit prose structure and do not execute commands or interpolate user input.
Lines 77-83 show inline code placeholders such as parameter and exception names inside a documentation template. They are formatting markers, not executable shell syntax.
Lines 83-91 continue the fenced Markdown reference template and close the code block. The content is a documentation skeleton with no command invocation.
Line 49 asks documentation authors to list default values and valid ranges for configuration options. This is reference content guidance, not system reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Reference gaps make APIs hard to adopt and maintain. This skill creates complete, searchable documentation for APIs, configuration, schemas, and error behavior.
actual_capabilities: Structures API references with methods, parameters, return values, errors, and examples.
Builds configuration guides with defaults, valid ranges, dependencies, and migration notes.
Documents schemas with field types, constraints, relationships, indexes, and version history.
Adds navigation aids such as tables of contents, indexes, categories, and cross-references.
Defines quality checks for completeness, accuracy, consistency, searchability, and maintainability.
limitations: It depends on accurate source material from the user or repository.
It does not verify behavior by running tests or inspecting live services by itself.
It can draft OpenAPI or schema metadata, but source truth must be reviewed.
It is not a substitute for product owner approval of public documentation.

use_cases.title: Document a New API
use_cases.description: Create a complete reference with endpoint behavior, parameters, return values, errors, examples, and related links.

use_cases.title: Standardize Configuration Docs
use_cases.description: Turn scattered settings into a searchable guide with defaults, valid values, dependencies, and upgrade notes.

use_cases.title: Prepare Release Documentation
use_cases.description: Build versioned reference material that explains changed interfaces, deprecated options, migration paths, and compatibility limits.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Reference
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single API or module.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a reference for this API. Include methods, parameters, returns, errors, examples, and a short index. Use the source files I provide.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Configuration Guide
prompt_templates.prompt: Document these configuration options. Include defaults, valid ranges, environment differences, dependencies, deprecated options, and migration guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Reference Completeness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this reference for gaps. Identify missing parameters, unclear defaults, weak examples, missing errors, and cross-references that should be added.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Versioned Reference Set
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced documentation architecture for a large product.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a versioned reference structure for this product. Include navigation, schema sections, compatibility matrices, deprecation policy, and validation checks.

output_examples.input: A request to document a payment API from source files and notes.
output: A method-by-method reference with parameters, return values, errors, and authentication details.
Examples for common payments, refunds, failures, and idempotency handling.
Cross-references to rate limits, security notes, and related configuration.

output_examples.input: A request to organize configuration settings for a deployment tool.
output: A searchable configuration guide grouped by environment, scope, and dependency.
Tables covering defaults, accepted values, required status, and version changes.
Migration notes for renamed, deprecated, or incompatible options.

best_practices: Provide source files, existing docs, and known edge cases before asking for a complete reference.
Ask for explicit sections when you need parameters, errors, examples, migrations, or compatibility matrices.
Review generated references against implementation details before publishing them.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to invent missing API behavior without source evidence.
Do not publish generated examples before checking that they match the real product.
Do not use it for broad tutorials when users need a concise reference.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create technical references for APIs, configuration options, schemas, errors, examples, and versioned behavior.

faq.question: Can it document existing code?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the relevant files or excerpts so it can extract interfaces, parameters, and constraints.

faq.question: Does it generate tutorials?
faq.answer: It focuses on reference documentation. It can include quick starts and examples when they support lookup tasks.

faq.question: Can it create searchable documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It emphasizes indexes, tables of contents, category grouping, aliases, and cross-references.

faq.question: Does it validate documentation accuracy?
faq.answer: It can define review checks, but humans should verify details against source code, tests, and product behavior.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
